newsitem.title: USA: ITT selling 5 Sheraton hotels for $200 million.
newsitem.headline: ITT selling 5 Sheraton hotels for $200 million.

text.p: ITT Corp., which is trying to thwart a $6.5 billion hostile takeover by Hilton Hotels Corp. by selling assets, said Monday it would sell five ITT Sheraton hotels to FelCor Suites Hotels Inc. for $200 million in cash.

Under the agreement, ITT will continue to manage the hotels for 20 years and work with FelCor to identify other potential acquisitions. FelCor wants to buy existing Sheraton hotels and convert others to the Sheraton brand.

The hotels, with more than 1,800 rooms in total, are Sheraton Gateway Hotel Atlanta Airport in College Park, Ga., Sheraton Suites Galleria in Atlanta, Sheraton Gateway Suites O'Hare Airport in Rosemont, Ill., Sheraton Crescent Hotel in Phoenix and Sheraton Park Central in Dallas.
ITT said it expects the transaction to close by the end of June. FelCor, based in Irving, Texas, said it will raise the $200 million in a securities offering.

The move is ITT's latest to try to fend off Hilton's bid by selling assets, but the biggest part of its defence strategy lies ahead. ITT is expected to generate more than $2 billion in coming months by selling assets, including a telephone directory business and an educational services unit.

Although most of the expected asset sales are non-core hotel and casino properties, the hotels in the latest deal are smaller than ITT's major Sheraton properties and considered to be in secondary markets for ITT. The move is expected to help ITT focus on giant properties that generate more income.
"In no way is this a departure from our goal to grow the Sheraton name," said ITT spokesman Jim Gallagher.
But the proposed transaction drew fire from Hilton, which said it represented ITT's desire to discourage its offer at all costs.
"It's just another sign of a purely entrenched management that is making moves, not toward creating shareholder value, but with an eye toward driving us away," said Hilton spokesman Marc Grossman.
He said that although the sale was "a disturbing signal", Hilton has no plans to revise its bid based on the asset sale.

Hilton launched its unsolicited $55-a-share bid in January. Since then, ITT has announced the sale of its stake in French telecommunications company Alcatel Alsthom, its 50 percent stake in Madison Square Garden to partner Cablevision Systems Corp. for $650 million and its 50 percent stake in television station WBIS to Paxson Communications Corp.

"ITT has been very successful thus far in its manoeuvres and I think it will continue in the same path," said Cowen & Co. analyst Harold Vogel, who recently raised his 12-month target price on ITT to $70 a share from $65.

Sources close to ITT said the Desert Inn in Las Vegas and its riverboat casino in Tunica, Miss., probably were next in line to be sold for about $400 million. The company has said potential buyers have expressed interest.

TT has not disclosed how it will use the proceeds from all the asset sales, but is widely expected to authorise a stock buyback or offer a special dividend to shareholders. Industry experts expect the move to come next fall before ITT battles Hilton in a proxy fight at ITT's annual meeting.
Hilton has proposed a slate of nominees to unseat ITT's board. ITT has not yet set a date for the meeting, but it is expected to be held in the fall.
ITT was unchanged at $59.375, FelCor was unchanged at $36.50 and Hilton added 37.5 cents to $29.75, all on the New York Stock Exchange.
